title: Drop VAT collection by online marketplaces
headline: Drop marketplace VAT rule. Costs £0.3bn in 2029-30.
description: From October 2027 online marketplaces must collect and pay the VAT on sales by UK sellers through their platforms, where a seller’s sales on the platform pass £90,000. Switch this on to drop the rule and give up what the Treasury scores for it.

baselinePolicy.text: Online marketplace VAT liability extends to UK sellers from 1 October 2027 (Table 6.1 line 46).

source.quote: requiring online marketplaces to collect and remit VAT on business-to-consumer sales by UK sellers through their platforms

alreadyIncludes: Online marketplace VAT liability extends to UK sellers from 1 October 2027 (Table 6.1 line 46).

lines.title: Online Marketplace Liability: Extend to UK businesses with a minimum annual sales threshold per platform of £90,000 from 1 October 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.
The OBR rates this costing as highly uncertain: it depends on how much VAT the sellers it catches would otherwise have paid (October 2026 outlook, Table 3.3).

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
